what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from El Salvador in the United States: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 95932 Salvadoran asylum seekers in the United States, 88.6% of all asylum seekers from El Salvador.
Refugees from El Salvador, a separate group, live mostly in the United States and Mexico.

why.text: The fact pack records no armed conflict and no dated events for El Salvador, so it does not say why people left.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2000 to 2004 and 2017 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2000 at its highest point, 176197 asylum seekers.
The figure fell to a low in 2010 and then rose again in the following years.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the United States.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for the United States only.
